nodes.label: D1 Cash View
nodes.rationale: A refund reduces profit in the period it was issued, using refund.processed_at. Past periods never change. The accrual alternative was rejected because it would rewrite the order's period when a refund arrives. The REFUND transaction timestamp is never used.

nodes.label: D2 Counted Orders
nodes.rationale: Only PAID, PARTIALLY_REFUNDED, and REFUNDED count, because money was collected. Pending, authorized, partially paid, voided, expired, cancelled-unpaid, and test orders are awaiting payment. Counting every non-cancelled order like Shopify analytics would overstate profit.

nodes.label: D3 Shopify Cost Is Estimated
nodes.rationale: Shopify stores only the current unit cost, so applying it to an old order may be wrong. A merchant cost with an effective date is Actual. Shopify's current cost on a past order is Estimated. No cost is Missing. Treating Shopify's cost as Actual was rejected because it misleads after cost changes.

nodes.label: D4 Missing Data Is Never Zero
nodes.rationale: No fee rule, shipping rule, or unit cost leaves the component Missing and the profit partial. Defaulting silently to zero was rejected because profit would look better than it is. A missing cost must not be called a confirmed loss.

nodes.label: D5 Profit Confidence
nodes.rationale: High, Medium, and Low measure data completeness, not statistical probability. Weights are 60 percent product cost, 20 percent fees, and 20 percent shipping. High is at least 0.90 and Medium at least 0.60. A numeric percentage was rejected as false precision.

nodes.label: D6 Gift Cards
nodes.rationale: Gift cards are a liability until redeemed, so gift-card product lines are excluded from sales and shown separately rather than treated as normal revenue.

nodes.label: D7 USD to AED Peg
nodes.rationale: The AED peg is 3.6725 per USD and is marked Actual. Every other pair needs a daily rate on the entry date, marked Estimated. A missing rate makes the converted value Missing, never 1.0. Original amount and currency are never overwritten.

nodes.label: D8 Variant Cost Granularity
nodes.rationale: Product cost is stored per variant with an effective date and applies until the next entry. Per-product storage was rejected because variants can be priced differently.

nodes.label: Business Date processed_at
nodes.rationale: The business date is processed_at in the shop time zone. Daily and monthly totals sum ledger entries by that date. The rate used for conversion is the rate on the entry date, not today's rate.

nodes.label: COGS Resolution
nodes.rationale: Cost per unit is the latest merchant cost with effective_from on or before the business date. Otherwise Shopify's current unit cost is Estimated. Otherwise the line is Missing. Lines without a cost contribute 0 to COGS and still count in the missing share. A change does not silently rewrite historical profit.

nodes.label: f_product_cost
nodes.rationale: Append-only per-variant cost history with who, when, and why. Entries can be revoked, not edited. Rows are keyed by Shopify variant id so a deleted variant keeps its merchant cost. Historical cost changes are seeded here, not in Shopify.

nodes.label: s_payment_fee_rule
nodes.rationale: Actual fee is what Shopify Payments reports. Otherwise the merchant rule is percentage plus fixed amount, rounded, and marked Estimated. If neither exists the fee is Missing. Refunds do not reduce a fixed fee.

nodes.label: s_shipping_cost_rule
nodes.rationale: Shopify does not report carrier cost, so shipping cost comes from an effective-dated merchant rule. Free-shipping orders can still cost money to ship. No rule is Missing. An explicit 0 is Actual-by-declaration. Nothing to ship is not applicable.

nodes.label: Component Status Model
nodes.rationale: Every ledger component is Actual, Estimated, Missing, or Not applicable. Aggregates carry the weakest status of their parts. The UI always shows which part is which so an estimate is not presented as an exact fact.

nodes.label: Profit Ledger
nodes.rationale: One entry per component per event stores order id, event date, signed shop-currency amount, status, source, inputs, and engine_version. Every dashboard number can be listed back to entries. Results are recomputed idempotently per order after a sync, webhook, or cost or rule change.

nodes.label: Golden Tests
nodes.rationale: Section 14 examples come from the seeded dev store, not invented numbers. The engine must reproduce them exactly. pnpm profit:verify re-checks them against the live dev store.
